title: WP05.12 -- idle class-weight profile at the same 52.5k beta=0.5 data and the same 5,000-step budget
one_line: same data / same budget / same seed as the WP05.8 5k arm, only the idle loss weight changed (idle weight 0.7129, effective idle share 44.00 %): 0/20 clears, frames mean 1693.30, idle 59.77 %
question: IDLE_DIAG.md says 66.16 % of the teacher labels are idle, 67.38 % of those come from 18-way ties, and dev idle (60.87 %) already sits on the label prior (61.72 %).  Does down-weighting the idle class at a fixed budget move the closed loop, or is the idle prior not the binding constraint?

fixed: the WP05.8 converted labels (byte-identical, SHA verified)

class_weight.normalisation: weights = multipliers / sum_c(prior_c * multiplier_c), so sum_c(prior_c * weights_c) == 1: the mean per-sample loss weight is 1 and the loss scale is comparable to --class-weight-mode none
class_weight.loss: per-row chosen one-hot CE times weights[target], normalised by the batch's weight mass sum_i weights[target_i] (a weighted mean)

rules.note: the class weight is a loss weight only; the streams, the shuffle, the batch composition and the labels are the pre-WP05.12 ones

prior_counts.source: expected class counts of the fixed-step stream: s1_quota * s1_frequency + dagger_quota * dagger_frequency
prior_counts.note: the loss sees weights[target], so this prior -- not a resampled count -- is what the class weight and the implied share describe

metrics.confusion_matrix_orientation: rows = target action, columns = predicted action

label_rule.note: chosen one-hot CE only; the other 17 logits appear solely in the softmax denominator

weighted_loss.objective: sum_i weights[target_i] * CE_i / sum_i weights[target_i] (the term this run optimised)
weighted_loss.unweighted_counterpart: metrics.loss / loss_first_step / loss_last_step / loss_first_100 / loss_last_100 are the unweighted chosen one-hot CE, so they are comparable with --class-weight-mode none

gpu.peak_memory_note: torch.cuda.max_memory_{allocated,reserved} over this run; reset immediately before the first step

mix.rule: per-step cumulative allocation floor((step+1)*steps*batch*share) - floor(step*steps*batch*share) S1 rows; per-class loss weights (class_weight.weights), no resampling; the batch order is shuffled per step, so the mix is the only source signal

not_claimed_as_written_by_the_tool: not the 50k-decision first DAgger round: this smoke trains 1,000 steps on the six completed shards (21,000 decisions, ~42 % of the 50k target)
not a β=0.5 round: every shard here used β=1.0 (full teacher injection)
not G410-2: no confirm-split run, no 20-episode protocol, no four-arm matrix
not a development score: the offline metrics are in-sample on the exact train batches this run consumed, so they are optimisation diagnostics, not held-out skill
no new data collection and no engine run: the game is never launched by this module; the two dev episodes are a separate evaluator invocation
one model arm (B0), one seed (0), one fixed step budget (1,000): no variance estimate and no convergence claim
rows without a chosen plan are excluded, and unknown candidates are never negative labels; that rule is not a learned preference over unknowns
a class weight is a loss weight only: no row is resampled, relabelled, reordered or dropped, and it adds no data and no teacher signal

window_alignment.training_window: the D410-S1 shards store frames[t-3..t], four consecutive game frames; one decision = two frames = two renders, so the stack is consecutive

wilson_95.basis: all scheduled episodes; a failed episode counts as a non-clear

verdict.what_this_is: smoke: the v410 checkpoint ran in the real engine under the S1N dev ruler

comparison.basis: the same 15 beta=0.5 round-2 shards, the same converted labels, the same 20 % / 80 % mix, the same optimiser/seed and the same 5,000-step budget; the single changed variable is the idle loss weight

contention.what: round3 DAgger batchA (tools/rl/v410_dagger_collect.py, seeds 2040-2054, beta=0.5) was running for the whole train + dev window; it was only observed, never signalled or killed
contention.note: the engine is stepped at a fixed frame budget, not in real time, so wall times and throughput absorb the contention but the episode frame counts do not depend on it

checks: weight table is 18-way, mean sample weight == 1
evaluated checkpoint SHA == the trained checkpoint SHA

verification.note: this builder raises instead of writing the file when any join above fails

limits: one arm (B0), one training seed (0), one step budget (5,000): no variance estimate, no interval and no ranking
one weight setting (idle target 0.44): this is a single point on the weight axis, not a sweep; nothing here says 0.44 is optimal
offline loss/top1/macroR are in-sample train-batch metrics, not held-out accuracy
the comparison with the 5k none arm is controlled on data/mix/budget/seed, but both arms share one training seed, so a 20-episode delta cannot be separated from seed noise

a class weight cannot add a state the corpus never visited: if the idle prior comes from tied teacher scores on states the student loops in, a loss weight does not change those states
round3 DAgger collection ran concurrently (observed, never killed): wall times and throughput are not comparable across rounds
